thresholdRule: For a lower limit, take the 5th percentile of the class's scans; for an upper limit, the 95th. When the measured stand-in nearest to the scans lies beyond that percentile by at least the measure's step (0.01 for D, 0.001 for solidity and shares, 0.1 degrees for p90), the threshold is the midpoint between the two, rounded to the step, and the measure separates the class. Otherwise the threshold is the percentile and the measure does not separate the class: a stand-in reaches the scans, or no stand-in has a value. A measure also separates only when at least 90 % of the class's scans have a value, so that no default rests on a minority of the scans. Only separating measures become defaults.
